title: In the Archery Tournament (Ha Ka Iasiat Ha Ka Iathong)
khasi_title: Ha Ka Iasiat Ha Ka Iathong
cultural_context: Rousing traditional archery phawar chanted by archers and villagers around the circular grass target (Skum) during tournament contests, from 'Ki Sur Ba Dang Sawa'.

khasi: Hoi-kiw! Ha ka iasiat ha ka iathong,
Ki ranglieng ki ieng beit thik;
Ka ryntieh siej-lieng ba la pynkhreh,
U khnam u her kum ka leilieh;
U sam beit ha u skum ba la buh,
Ki kynhun ki risaw da ka jingkmen;
Dei ka bor ka kti bad ka jingshai ka khmat
Ba ai nam ia u samla ba shlur.
english: Hoi-kiw! In the contest of the flying arrows,
The archers stand straight and steady;
The bow of seasoned bamboo drawn tight,
The feather-fletched arrow flies swift as lightning;
Striking dead center into the woven grass target,
The cheering village rings out in triumph;
It is the steady hand and sharp, keen eye
That wins renown for the courageous youth.

khasi: Phawar, ko paralok, phawar da ka hok,
Wat kren ia ka ktien ba pynshun;
Kam dei ban pynpait ia ka shnong;
Hynrei ban pynkhlain ia ka met,
Ban pyniatylli ia ki kur ki kha,
Ban ri ia ka akor u kpa tymmen
english: Chant your phawar, comrades, chant with sporting honor,
Utter no harsh word that breeds hostility;
The archery of the Seven Huts
Is never meant to divide the village;
To bind together maternal and paternal kin,
To preserve the noble conduct of our ancestors
Until the sun sinks into dusk.

vocabulary.siej-lieng: indigenous mountain bamboo variety used for bows
